questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I just wanted to go on an exchange and try to live in another country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study calender and the reviews from other students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt recieve any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I became part of a MS Teams group made by WUR through which I found my accomodation. However, my rental contract expired with one month remaining of my semester, so I found housing through facebook groups and airbnb for the last month. This was a bit of a stressful situation.
I recommend signing up for
Room.nl
, ask WUR about the Teams group and to look at different facebook pages. Most rooms are only offered few weeks before you move in so it's important to keep your cool.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's totally fine to do. If you live in Wageningen you can get to campus in about 10-15 min.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was easy for the most part. 
I registered for two course that had a cap on the amount of participants and so I wasn't sure until quite close to the registration deadline whether I would be accepted to the course or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators were helpful and quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got accepted for all the classes that I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pay attention whether the course is a maximum participants course, if so, it's a good idea to have backup course ready.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is similar to UCPH but the courses can feel a bit more shallow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures are shorter. There are much more project work. There are fewer books and in some courses the curriculum consisted primarily of powerpoint slides, lectures and pdfs.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Bioinformatics, Introduction to Systems and Synthetic Biology, Genomics, Plant Biotechnology, Plants and Health.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked the Genomics. It was an interactive course with a lot of feedback from the teachers. 
The intro to systems and synthetic biology was also interesting but also very different from what I've tried before and we were just 10 students in the class.

questions.answer: Bike repairs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Being part of sportclub de bongerd was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
For athletic activites, there are lots of different sports to do at the sports de bongerd. 
For cultural and social activities, ESN and ISOW offer many events and trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to do a sport as it's fun, healthy and good way to meet people. 
I also recommend to be part of ESN and/or ISOW as this is a good way to get good experiences with other exchange and international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The national park Veluwe can be reached by bike. 
Cities within or outside of Netherlands can also be visited.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be difficult as the dutch students already have friend groups they like to hang out with. The best tip is to try and learn the language. The dutch like it when you try to speak it and it's not too difficult as it's similar to danish.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking culture. Everything is reachable within 10-15 minutes in Wageningen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take part in many social events, especially in the beginning. 
Be active in the house searching but also try to stay calm. 
Sign up for a sport.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a look around in the different buildings. I really liked the so-called "The Spot" in the Orion building.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting people from around the world. 
Being part of the football team GVC, being part of a buddy group through ESN and going to Paris with ESN.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Probably to find housing for the last month of my exchange. 
And to find the right balance between following the courses and having "non-academic" fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
